boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the three undrafted frozen records in the Maryland Campaign; MD003 Antietam keeps its existing draft unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates: Harpers Ferry September 12–15, South Mountain September 14 and Shepherdstown September 19–20. The live NPS campaign heading does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field says Brigades; the live field reads zero. Palfrey says volunteers from four regiments crossed on the 19th and a reconnaissance under Morell and Sykes on the 20th, and that nine or ten Confederate brigades took part.
claims.rationale: Two separate crossings with changing populations; no counts. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 625 total; the live NPS field reads 654 total (US 363; CS 291;). NPS gives 269 casualties in the 118th Pennsylvania; Palfrey says it lost 282 of 800, and rejects A. P. Hill's reported claim of 3,000 killed and drowned from one brigade.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. A. P. Hill's figure is an attributed claim quoted by Palfrey, not a loss count.

open_questions: Returns, casualty reconciliation and the division of the action between September 19 and 20 remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Palfrey is one retrospective history by a Union officer who served in the campaign and used advance sheets of the Official Records. Reports quoted inside Palfrey are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
